examples.claim: Waste confined to the last block, under 4%; 2–4x throughput over FasterTransformer/Orca at the same latency
examples.source: Blog: 'a mere waste of under 4%'; paper abstract: 'improves the throughput ... by 2-4× with the same level of latency compared to ... FasterTransformer and Orca'.

examples.claim: Against current engines the paper's 2–4x is the realistic starting point
examples.source: Paper compares only with FasterTransformer and Orca; no source compares current engines.

examples.claim: B=16, 50 tokens: 4 blocks, 14 empty slots; a 2048-token reservation leaves 1998 idle; the 60–80% waste comes exactly from such reservation
examples.source: Arithmetic right (ceil(50/16)=4, 64-50=14, 2048-50=1998), but blog: waste 'due to fragmentation and over-reservation'; the cause is narrowed.

examples.claim: PagedAttention kernel latency 20–26% higher than FasterTransformer's; only the attention operator is affected
examples.source: Paper §7.2: 'this leads to 20–26% higher attention kernel latency ... it only affects the attention operator but not the other operators'.

examples.claim: Third-party post: per-sequence waste at most 15 slots, the partly filled last block
examples.source: runpod: 'Fragmentation shrinks to a maximum of 15 wasted token slots per sequence (the partially filled last block)'.

examples.claim: Scheduler broadcasts token IDs and block tables to all workers; workers sync via all-reduce without the scheduler and return sampled tokens
examples.source: Paper §4.6: control message with input token IDs and block table broadcast; 'synchronize the intermediate results with the all-reduce communication primitive without the coordination of the scheduler'; 'send the sampled tokens ... back to the scheduler'.

examples.claim: In vLLM, CoW applies only when new tokens fall in an old shared block, copying one block
examples.source: Paper §4.4: 'The copy-on-write mechanism is applied only when the newly generated tokens are within an old shared block ... This involves only copying one block of data.'

examples.claim: A third-party post on V1 reports hash-based prefix caching + LRU in V0 and V1, <1% throughput loss at 0% hit rate, default on in V1 and off in V0
examples.source: Numbers match the official vLLM blog (2025-01-27 V1 alpha release by the vLLM team), which the post calls third-party; misattribution.

examples.claim: Budget 2,048: A, B, C 1 token each, D 2,045 of a 3,000-token prompt; next iteration D 955, total 958
examples.source: Writer's labelled example ('가정합니다'); code block runs (assert holds); 3000-2045=955; 3+955=958; V1 guide: '{request_id: num_tokens} to dynamically allocate a fixed token budget'.

examples.claim: FCFS for all requests, latest-arrived preempted first; all-or-nothing eviction; gang-scheduled sequence groups
examples.source: Paper §4.5: 'the earliest arrived requests are served first and the latest requests are preempted first'; 'all-or-nothing eviction policy'; 'gang-scheduled as a sequence group'.

examples.claim: Swap re-admission can take hundreds of ms
examples.source: runpod scopes it: 'On a PCIe 4.0 x16 link (~32 GB/s), restoring a long-context sequence on Llama-3-70B can take hundreds of milliseconds'; the post drops the scope.

examples.claim: V1 rewrote scheduler, KV cache manager, worker, sampler, API server; V1 alpha up to 1.7x over V0 without multi-step scheduling on Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.3 70B and Qwen2-VL
examples.source: v0.8.1 V1 guide: 're-architects ... the scheduler, KV cache manager, worker, sampler, and API server'; V1 alpha blog: 'up to 1.7x higher throughput compared to V0 (without multi-step scheduling)', Llama 3.1 8B & 3.3 70B, Qwen2-VL on VisionArena.

examples.claim: Binaries built with CUDA 12.9 by default; 12.8 and 13.0 builds available; Blackwell needs CUDA 12.8+
examples.source: GPU page: 'compiled with CUDA 12.9 ... by default. We also provide vLLM binaries compiled with CUDA 12.8, 13.0'; 'NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (B200, GB200) require a minimum of CUDA 12.8'.

examples.claim: Quickstart: ROCm wheels support Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0, glibc >= 2.35; GPU page: ROCm 6.3+ (MI350 7.0+)
examples.source: Quickstart: 'It currently supports Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0 and glibc >= 2.35'; GPU page: 'ROCm 6.3 or above', 'MI350 requires ROCm 7.0 or above' (the GPU page now builds wheels for ROCm 10.0, not mentioned).

examples.claim: '8k' is 8,000 and '32K' is 32,768 tokens, a 768-token difference
examples.source: CLI page: '1k = 1,000 (decimal kilo) 1K = 1,024'; exercised: human_readable_int('8k')=8000, ('32K')=32768; make_arg_parser gives max_num_batched_tokens 8000, max_model_len 32768.

off_sample_findings.claim: The 55% memory saving is what the 3-parallel-completion HF/TGI benchmark numbers measure
off_sample_findings.source: Blog: 'cutting their memory usage by up to 55%. This can translate into up to 2.2x improvement in throughput.' The 8.5–15x / 3.3–3.5x figures compare whole systems; the blog does not attribute them to sharing.

off_sample_findings.claim: nm-vllm 0.5.0 docs say the KV cache block count is affected by --gpu-memory-utilization
off_sample_findings.source: nm-vllm 0.5.0 engine_args: only 'The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model executor ... Default: 0.9' and '--num-gpu-blocks-override: If specified, ignore GPU profiling result'; no statement about block count.

off_sample_findings.claim: If the preemption counter keeps rising, lower --max-num-seqs, add KV capacity or add instances
off_sample_findings.source: runpod 'vLLM Explained': 'If ... vllm:num_preemptions_total grows steadily under nominal load, you need to reduce --max-model-len, raise --gpu-memory-utilization, or add capacity'; --max-num-seqs is not named.

off_sample_findings.claim: A steadily rising preemption counter means the batch cap is high relative to KV cache capacity
off_sample_findings.source: No source states this cause; runpod calls sustained preemption a degradation state and lists other remedies.

off_sample_findings.claim: VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE default 0 means the variable does not override the size
off_sample_findings.source: CPU page: 'Default value is 0.' only; source vllm/envs.py: unset -> None with comment 'default is None and will be set as 4 GB'. The 'does not override' meaning is the writer's.
Docker docs: 'You can either use the ipc=host flag or --shm-size flag'; the post's next sentence says the same, so the first sentence overstates.
